import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.ExteriorPower.Basis
import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Dual.Basis

/-!
# Exterior powers of the dual and alternating forms

The canonical determinant pairing identifies the exterior power of the dual
of a finite free module with alternating forms on that module. This is the
linear algebra in Mumford's description of integral torus cohomology.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

noncomputable section

namespace Mumford.Analytic

variable {R M : Type*} [CommRing R] [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]

/-- Wedges of a finite dual basis pair as the dual exterior basis. -/
theorem exteriorPowerPairingDual_basis {I : Type*} [LinearOrder I] [Finite I]
    (b : Module.Basis I R M) (n : ℕ) (s : Set.powersetCard I n) :
    exteriorPower.pairingDual R M n (b.dualBasis.exteriorPower n s) =
      (b.exteriorPower n).dualBasis s := by
  rw [show (b.exteriorPower n).dualBasis s = (b.exteriorPower n).coord s from
    congrFun (Module.Basis.coe_dualBasis (b.exteriorPower n)) s]
  rw [exteriorPower.basis_coord, exteriorPower.ιMultiDual,
    exteriorPower.basis_apply, Module.Basis.coe_dualBasis]

/-- The determinant pairing is bijective for a module with a finite basis. -/
theorem exteriorPowerPairingDual_bijective_of_basis
    {I : Type*} [LinearOrder I] [Finite I] (b : Module.Basis I R M) (n : ℕ) :
    Function.Bijective (exteriorPower.pairingDual R M n) := by
  let e := (b.dualBasis.exteriorPower n).equiv (b.exteriorPower n).dualBasis
    (Equiv.refl (Set.powersetCard I n))
  have he : e.toLinearMap = exteriorPower.pairingDual R M n := by
    apply (b.dualBasis.exteriorPower n).ext
    intro s
    change e (b.dualBasis.exteriorPower n s) = _
    rw [exteriorPowerPairingDual_basis]
    exact Module.Basis.equiv_apply _ _ _ _
  rw [← he]
  exact e.bijective

variable (R M) [Module.Free R M] [Module.Finite R M]

/-- The canonical pairing of exterior powers is bijective for finite free modules. -/
theorem exteriorPowerPairingDual_bijective (n : ℕ) :
    Function.Bijective (exteriorPower.pairingDual R M n) := by
  classical
  letI : LinearOrder (Module.Free.ChooseBasisIndex R M) :=
    linearOrderOfSTO WellOrderingRel
  exact exteriorPowerPairingDual_bijective_of_basis (Module.Free.chooseBasis R M) n

/-- The canonical exterior pairing, as an equivalence for finite free modules. -/
def exteriorPowerDualEquiv (n : ℕ) :
    (⋀[R]^n (Module.Dual R M)) ≃ₗ[R] Module.Dual R (⋀[R]^n M) :=
  LinearEquiv.ofBijective (exteriorPower.pairingDual R M n)
    (exteriorPowerPairingDual_bijective R M n)

@[simp]
theorem exteriorPowerDualEquiv_toLinearMap (n : ℕ) :
    (exteriorPowerDualEquiv R M n).toLinearMap = exteriorPower.pairingDual R M n := rfl

/-- Alternating forms on a finite free module are exterior products of its dual. -/
def exteriorPowerDualAlternatingEquiv (n : ℕ) :
    (⋀[R]^n (Module.Dual R M)) ≃ₗ[R] AlternatingMap R M R (Fin n) :=
  (exteriorPowerDualEquiv R M n).trans exteriorPower.alternatingMapLinearEquiv.symm

/-- Evaluation of the alternating-form equivalence is the canonical exterior pairing. -/
@[simp]
theorem exteriorPowerDualAlternatingEquiv_apply (n : ℕ)
    (x : ⋀[R]^n (Module.Dual R M)) (v : Fin n → M) :
    exteriorPowerDualAlternatingEquiv R M n x v =
      exteriorPower.pairingDual R M n x (exteriorPower.ιMulti R n v) := by
  rw [exteriorPowerDualAlternatingEquiv, LinearEquiv.trans_apply,
    exteriorPower.alternatingMapLinearEquiv_symm_apply]
  rfl

/-- A wedge of linear forms evaluates as the determinant of their values. -/
@[simp]
theorem exteriorPowerDualAlternatingEquiv_ιMulti (n : ℕ)
    (f : Fin n → Module.Dual R M) (v : Fin n → M) :
    exteriorPowerDualAlternatingEquiv R M n (exteriorPower.ιMulti R n f) v =
      Matrix.det (Matrix.of (fun i j => f j (v i))) := by
  rw [exteriorPowerDualAlternatingEquiv_apply, exteriorPower.pairingDual_ιMulti_ιMulti]

end Mumford.Analytic
